Overall: 5/10.

Story & Plot

On a perilous climb across Mount Kwan in Thailand, two climbers named Jax and Luce attempt to conquer a treacherous plank walk. However, a sudden rock slide leaves them trapped thousands of feet above the ground at a terrifying height of 3,000 feet. Sheer exposure, vertigo-inducing heights, and impossible odds turn every moment into a desperate fight for survival as they are forced to cooperate.

Comedy & Entertainment

As a survival thriller directed by Peter Spierig, the film is not designed to offer humor or comedic moments. Instead, its entertainment value relies heavily on whether its popcorn thriller formula and adrenaline-fueled suspense can keep audiences engaged. While some viewers find enough nail-biting sequences and edge-of-the-seat moments to watch, others note it lacks traditional comedic relief or lighthearted breaks.

Performances & Direction

The cast features Harriet Slater, Arsema Thomas, Tom Brittney, Sahajak Boonthanakit, and Korakod Yensuk. Reviewers highlight that the actors deliver committed performances while navigating their characters' high-stakes dilemma, bringing enough ingenuity and chutzpah to make the perilous situation somewhat compelling.

Strengths

  • Vertigo-inducing visuals
  • Committed performances from the cast
  • Adrenalised editing and cool camera tricks
  • Breathless edge-of-the-seat escape moments

Weaknesses

The film suffers from a predictable story that follows a basic formula, alongside less convincing special effects, really poor CG environments, and visually uninteresting elements. Some critics also point to poorly paced sequences, horrendous ADR, and characters making non-sensical decisions that ultimately lead to a bizarre ending.

Final verdict

Fall 2: Deadpoint functions as a decent popcorn thriller for fans of extreme survival premises, but it struggles under the weight of a familiar formula and uneven production qualities. While it offers a handful of harrowing sequences and committed acting, its exhausting pacing and weak second half make it a mixed experience. Viewers seeking high-altitude thrills may find intermittent entertainment, but many will likely be disappointed by its shortcomings.
